submitted.rationale: Of the three compositions measured, index 7 (Mg 0.57) gave the highest photocurrent, 2e-8 A. It sits in the Mg7Mn5O12-like mixed region, where the predicted gap (2.7 eV) is small enough to absorb 3.22 eV light.

rejected.reason: Measured 0 A, even though the MgMn2O4 spinel is stable and its predicted 2.87 eV gap should absorb this light
Measured -1e-8 A; the predicted gap (~3.3 eV) is at or above the 3.22 eV photon energy
Not measured; the phases predicted there (Mn3O4, MgMn6O12) have small gaps of 0.9-1.4 eV and are unlikely photoanodes

consultations.verdict: Support: MgMn2O4 spinel is on hull (MACE Ehull 0) with HSE gap 2.87 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; Mg6MnO8 (3.74 eV) would not absorb, Mn3O4 (0.94 eV) likely poor. Index 16 (Mg 0.32) is closest to spinel stoichiometry.

Moderate support: spinel region gave zero. Mg7Mn5O12 (Mg 0.58) HSE gap 2.71 eV absorbs 3.22 eV light; Mg8Mn3O11 at 3.32 eV borderline; Mn-rich MgMn6O12 1.42 eV small gap. Index 7 (Mg 0.57) probes the Mg-rich mixed region.

Weak support: Mg8Mn3O11 (Mg 0.727) is near-hull (0.027 eV/atom) with gap ~3.3 eV near photon energy; photocurrent rose from 0 at Mg 0.32 to 2e-8 A at Mg 0.57, so moving Mg-richer toward ~0.71 is the best remaining bet.
